mainTopic: Moving מוקצה that rests on permitted objects on שבת: the stone on the barrel, coins on the cushion, and the loaf-or-baby method
overview: The amud opens by settling an apparent dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר about a מדומע mixture: both agree a mental choice is enough, and רבי יהודה simply goes further. Then a new משנה teaches how to deal with מוקצה resting on permitted things on שבת. A stone on a barrel is tipped off, coins on a cushion are shaken off, and bird droppings are wiped with a rag, or washed with water if the cushion is leather. רב limits these leniencies to an item that was forgotten there; if it was placed on purpose, the base becomes a בסיס לדבר האסור. The גמרא shows that the barrel rule follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, comparing the stone to waste that blocks the food. It also teaches that if one needs only the cushion's place, he may move it with the coins still on it. Several אמוראים allow moving a forgotten purse, brick or saddlebag by placing a loaf or a baby on it. מר זוטרא limits this to forgotten items, and רב אשי limits it to a dead body. רב יוסף mocks אביי and רבא for using the method on purpose, and each answers that the item was usable for ordinary people and he needed the utensil only because of his status. The amud ends by asking whether רבא follows רבי יהודה, citing his instruction to throw a duck's intestines to the cat.

steps.title: Don't these two תנאים disagree about the mixture?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the link it just made between רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and רבי יהודה. It quotes a ברייתא where they seem to disagree about how to fix a מדומע mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't he disagree with him? As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says one lifts out the תרומה from a mixture of 101 parts. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says one looks at one side of the pile in his mind and eats from the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own earlier assumption that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר agrees with רבי יהודה. It brings a ברייתא where they seem to argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one measure of תרומה falls into 100 measures of חולין, it is nullified, but one measure must still be taken out for a כהן. רבי יהודה speaks of physically lifting a measure out. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says a mental choice is enough. So it looks like they disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that…? (opens a challenge)
A mixture of תרומה and ordinary produce (חולין)
One lifts out (removes the תרומה portion)
One part in 101 (the ratio for nullifying תרומה)
He sets his eyes on, i.e., designates in his mind

steps.confusionAlert: Lifting out the measure here does not mean the תרומה stops being nullified. The mixture is already permitted by the ratio. The only question is how one fulfills the duty to set aside one measure for the כהן.

phrases.english: But doesn't he disagree with him?
As it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One lifts out the teruma from a mixture of one hundred and one.
phrases.notes: One measure of תרומה mixed into 100 measures of חולין.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
He sets his eyes on this side
phrases.notes: He decides in his mind that the measure for the כהן is on this side.

phrases.english: and eats from a different side.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִיפְלָג פְּלִיג עִילָּוֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier claim (on the previous amud) that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר agrees with רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds like רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows them giving different methods: physically lifting out versus a mental choice. That suggests a real disagreement.

steps.title: רבי יהודה just goes further
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two do not really disagree. רבי יהודה's view simply goes further than רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה's view goes further than רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Both agree that a mental choice is enough, and רבי יהודה adds something more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that thought alone fixes the mixture. רבי יהודה adds that because thought is enough, physically lifting out the measure does not count as 'fixing' the food. So one may lift it out even on שבת. The earlier link between them stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes further; is a stronger, more far-reaching position

steps.whatToRemember: There is no argument between them. Both say a mental choice is enough. רבי יהודה adds that lifting the measure out on שבת is fine, because it is not an act of fixing the food.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda's view goes further
than Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה עֲדִיפָא מִדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the apparent disagreement is really agreement, with one view going further
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the two disagreed about whether thought alone is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree thought is enough. רבי יהודה goes further and allows physical lifting even on שבת, since it does not fix the food.

steps.title: A stone resting on a barrel
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. A stone (מוקצה) sitting on a barrel is removed by tilting the barrel so the stone slides off. If other barrels are nearby, one first lifts the barrel away from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A stone on the mouth of a barrel: one tilts the barrel on its side, and the stone falls off. If the barrel was among other barrels, one lifts it, then tilts it on its side, and the stone falls off.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It teaches how to get to a permitted barrel when a מוקצה stone is resting on top of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stone is מוקצה, so one may not pick it up directly. Instead one moves the barrel, which is permitted, so the stone falls off by itself. If the stone might break nearby barrels, one is even allowed to lift the barrel, with the stone still on it, before tilting.

keyTerms.meaning: He tilts it on its side

steps.confusionAlert: Lifting the barrel while the stone is still on it does not mean one may carry מוקצה freely. It is allowed only because the person needs the barrel and the stone must not damage the other barrels.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A stone that is on the mouth of a barrel —
one tilts it on its side, and the stone falls.
If it was among the barrels —
phrases.notes: Letting the stone fall there could break the other barrels.

phrases.english: he lifts it and tilts it on its side,
and the stone falls.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאֶבֶן שֶׁעַל פִּי הֶחָבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה; it does not continue the מדומע discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מוקצה stone on a barrel is removed indirectly by tilting the barrel. If needed, one lifts the barrel away from other barrels first.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic method for מוקצה resting on a permitted object: move the permitted object, not the מוקצה.

steps.title: Coins lying on a cushion
steps.stepSummary: Coins (מוקצה) resting on a cushion are removed by shaking the cushion until they fall off.
steps.simpleTranslation: Coins on a cushion: one shakes the cushion, and they fall off.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second case of the same pattern: shake the permitted cushion so the מוקצה coins fall off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coins are מוקצה and may not be handled directly. The cushion is permitted, so one moves the cushion, and the coins drop by themselves. This follows the same logic as the stone on the barrel.

phrases.english: Coins that are on the cushion —
he shakes the cushion, and they fall.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָעוֹת שֶׁעַל הַכַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same indirect-removal method to a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coins on a cushion are removed by shaking the cushion.

steps.title: Cleaning bird droppings off a cushion
steps.stepSummary: Bird droppings on a cloth cushion are wiped off with a rag, not washed. A leather cushion may be washed with water, because laundering is not a concern for leather.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were bird droppings on it, one wipes them with a rag. If the cushion was made of leather, one pours water on it until the droppings are gone.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with how to clean dirt off a cushion on שבת. It makes a difference between cloth and leather.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting water on cloth counts as כיבוס (laundering), which is forbidden on שבת. That is why a cloth cushion may only be wiped with a dry rag. Water does not count as laundering leather, so a leather cushion may be rinsed until it is clean.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule is to remove מוקצה indirectly, by moving the permitted object it rests on (stone on barrel, coins on cushion). When cleaning, cloth may not get water because of כיבוס, but leather may.

phrases.english: If there was bird dung on it —
he wipes it with a rag.
phrases.notes: Not with water, because that would be laundering.

phrases.english: If it was made of leather —
one puts water on it until the dung is gone.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה עָלָיו לִשְׁלֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the cushion case with a new problem: dirt instead of מוקצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wipe droppings off cloth with a rag. Leather may be rinsed with water, because there is no כיבוס concern.

steps.title: רב limits the stone rule to a forgotten stone
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה's method of tilting the barrel applies only when the stone was forgotten on it. If the owner deliberately placed the stone there, the barrel becomes a בסיס לדבר האסור and may not be moved at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: The משנה only taught this when the person forgot the stone there. But if he put it there on purpose, the barrel becomes a base for a forbidden object.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and adds an important limit to the משנה about the stone on the barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed tilting the barrel so the stone falls off. רב explains this is only true when the stone was forgotten. If the owner put the stone on the barrel before שבת on purpose, the barrel is treated as a holder of the מוקצה, so it becomes forbidden to move too.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of… (a formula that limits a law)
One who forgets (left it there by accident)
One who places (put it there on purpose)
A base for a forbidden item; the holder itself becomes מוקצה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the barrel is forbidden just because a stone is on it. It becomes a בסיס only if the stone was placed there on purpose. If the stone was forgotten, the barrel stays permitted and may be tilted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for the practical laws of בסיס לדבר האסור: what matters is whether the forbidden item was placed deliberately.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
They only taught this where one forgets (the stone)
phrases.notes: The משנה's permission applies only to a forgotten stone.

phrases.english: But where one places it (deliberately) —
(the barrel) becomes a base for a forbidden object.
phrases.notes: So the barrel itself may not be moved.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּשׁוֹכֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה's stone-on-barrel case (step 3) to a forgotten stone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tilting the barrel is permitted only if the stone was forgotten. A deliberately placed stone makes the barrel a בסיס לדבר האסור.

steps.title: Which תנא holds we exert effort with the permitted item?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a barrel among other barrels. It asks which תנא holds that we take extra effort with the permitted item rather than handle the forbidden item.
steps.simpleTranslation: (The משנה said:) 'If it was among the barrels…' Who is the תנא who holds that whenever there is a forbidden item and a permitted item, we go to the trouble with the permitted one, and do not go to the trouble with the forbidden one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks who the source is. It is setting up the next move, where it will name the תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting the barrel away from the others is more work than just picking up the stone. Still, the משנה requires the harder path so that the מוקצה stone is not handled directly. The גמרא wants to know which תנא holds this principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the Tanna (whose view this is)?
A forbidden item and a permitted item
We go to the trouble; we exert ourselves

phrases.english: [If it was among the barrels, etc.]
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: he lifts the barrel away first, then tilts it.

phrases.english: Who is the Tanna who holds that anywhere
that there is a forbidden item and a permitted item —
we exert ourselves with the permitted item,
phrases.notes: Here, lifting the barrel.

phrases.english: but we do not exert ourselves with the forbidden item?
phrases.notes: Here, picking up the stone, even though that would be easier.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא דְּכֹל הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא אִיסּוּרָא וְהֶיתֵּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the forgotten/placed limit to the משנה's next clause about a barrel among other barrels.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who prefers extra effort with a permitted item over handling a forbidden item.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: it is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by naming the תנא. It will prove this in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is short. It names רבן שמעון בן גמליאל but does not yet explain why. The proof follows from a case about sorting food on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often reports teachings of רבי יוחנן

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is (the view of) Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Background משנה: sorting legumes on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: To prove the answer, the גמרא first brings a משנה. In it, בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about how one may sort legumes on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One who sorts legumes on יום טוב — בית שמאי say: He picks out food and eats it. בית הלל say: He sorts in his usual way, in his lap or in a large dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings background text that it needs for the proof. This step sets up the next one, where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל comments on this dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בית שמאי, one may only pick out the good food bit by bit and eat it. According to בית הלל, one may sort in the normal way, even removing the waste. This dispute is the base that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל will limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Picks out food and eats it right away

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah: One who sorts legumes on a Festival,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: בּוֹרֵר אוֹכֶל וְאוֹכֵל.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: He selects food and eats it.
phrases.notes: Only picking out the food, little by little.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: He sorts in his usual manner,
phrases.notes: He may even remove the waste and leave the food.

phrases.english: in his lap or in a large dish.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַבּוֹרֵר קִטְנִית בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the proof for רבי יוחנן's answer in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the source of the משנה's rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about בית שמאי and בית הלל sorting legumes on יום טוב (background text).

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: when waste is the majority, take the food
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He says the dispute applies only when the food is the majority. When the waste is the majority, everyone agrees one picks out the food. This matches the משנה's rule of preferring the effort with the permitted item.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: When were these words said? When the food is more than the waste. But if the waste is more than the food, everyone agrees he picks out the food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's limit on the dispute shows that he is the one who holds the principle in the barrel משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the waste is the larger amount, everyone agrees one picks out the food, because that is the smaller job, and one does not have to work through the waste. The גמרא treats the stone like that waste: one deals with the permitted item and leaves the forbidden item alone, as with lifting the barrel instead of touching the stone. The next step asks whether the barrel case really fits 'waste is the majority.'

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught in a ברייתא
In what case were these words said? (a formula that limits a ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: when there is a choice between extra effort with a permitted item and handling a forbidden item, take the extra effort with the permitted item. So one lifts the barrel and does not pick up the stone.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is ruling on sorting in general. He only limits the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל to cases where the food is the majority. When the waste is the majority, everyone agrees one picks out the food and leaves the waste.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a general rule for מוקצה: extra effort with permitted items is preferred over handling forbidden ones.

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: And it was taught in a Baraita: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
In what case were these words (the dispute) said —
where the food is more than the waste.
But if the waste is more than the food —
everyone agrees he selects the food.
phrases.notes: He takes the food and leaves the larger amount of waste. This parallels dealing with the barrel rather than the stone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 9 by bringing רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's limit on that dispute.
steps.raayaObject: That the barrel משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that when waste is the majority, everyone agrees one picks out the food despite the extra effort.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The barrel משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: one takes the extra effort with the permitted item rather than handle the forbidden item.

steps.title: Isn't the barrel case like food being the majority?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The barrel is bigger than the stone, so the case looks like 'food is more than waste,' and in that case the rule is disputed rather than agreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, isn't it like a case where the food is more than the waste!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof it just brought. It says the barrel case does not seem to match the 'waste is the majority' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said everyone agrees to work with the food only when the waste is the majority. Here the barrel of wine (the permitted item) is much bigger than the one stone. So the case looks like 'food is the majority,' where בית הלל allow handling the waste directly. That would mean the משנה's rule does not clearly follow from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that… (opens a challenge)
Waste (the item one wants to get rid of)

phrases.english: But here,
phrases.notes: Refers to the barrel with the stone on it.

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי אוֹכֶל מְרוּבֶּה עַל הַפְּסוֹלֶת דָּמֵי!
phrases.english: it is like a case where the food is more than the waste!
phrases.notes: The barrel (food) is bigger than the stone (waste).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא, דְּכִי אוֹכֶל מְרוּבֶּה עַל הַפְּסוֹלֶת דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל brought in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's 'waste is the majority' case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Physically the barrel is bigger than the stone, so the case fits 'food is the majority.' רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gave no universal agreement for that case.

steps.title: The stone blocks the wine, so it counts as waste being the majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that size is not what matters here. The wine cannot be taken until the stone is removed, so the stone acts like a big obstacle. That makes the case like 'waste is the majority.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, since if he wants to take the wine, he cannot get the wine until he removes the stone, it is like a case where the waste is more than the food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the proof. It explains that the barrel case really does fit 'waste is the majority.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts is not physical size but how much the waste gets in the way. Since no wine can be reached at all without dealing with the stone, the stone acts like a lot of waste blocking the food. So רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's agreed rule applies: work with the permitted item, and the proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too (introduces an answer that fits the case into the rule)

steps.whatToRemember: The barrel case counts as 'waste is the majority' because the stone blocks all access to the wine. So the משנה fits רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: put the effort into the permitted item.

phrases.english: Here too,
since if he wants to take [the wine],
the wine cannot be taken by him
until he removes the stone,
it is like waste being more than the food.
phrases.notes: So everyone agrees to work with the permitted item.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּאִי בָּעֵי לְמִישְׁקַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: 'majority' is measured by how much the waste blocks the food, not by size.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bigger barrel makes this a case of food being the majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the stone blocks all the wine, it counts as waste being the majority, so the proof from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds.

steps.title: How to handle a barrel that cannot be tilted where it stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a barrel among other barrels. It brings a ברייתא of רבי יוסי: if the barrel is in a storeroom or has glass vessels under it, one lifts it to another spot, tilts it so the stone falls, takes what he needs, and puts it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If it was among the barrels, he lifts it.' It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי says: If the barrel was placed in a storeroom, or glass vessels were placed under it, he lifts it to another place, tilts it on its side, and the stone falls off. Then he takes from it what he needs and returns it to its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line about a barrel standing among other barrels, the same line discussed in steps 7–12. It brings a ברייתא that spells out exactly what to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tilting the barrel in place could break the other barrels or the glass under it. So רבי יוסי says to lift the barrel to a safe spot first, then tilt it so the stone falls. Throughout, one handles only the permitted barrel and never touches the stone directly, matching the principle from the earlier steps.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
He tilts it on its side

steps.confusionAlert: Lifting the barrel to another place does not mean carrying the stone around on purpose. The barrel is moved only so it can be tilted safely, and the stone just falls off. The stone itself is never picked up.

phrases.english: 'If it was among the barrels, he lifts it.'
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
If the barrel was placed in a storeroom,
phrases.notes: Among other barrels.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ כְּלֵי זְכוּכִית מוּנָּחִין תַּחְתֶּיהָ —
phrases.english: or glass vessels were placed beneath it,
phrases.notes: So tilting it in place could break things.

phrases.english: he lifts it to another place,
and tilts it on its side, and it [the stone] falls,
and he takes from it what he needs,
and returns it to its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה בֵּין הֶחָבִיּוֹת — מַגְבִּיהַּ. תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's clause about the barrel among other barrels, which step 7 already quoted, and brings רבי יוסי's ברייתא to explain it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the barrel cannot be tilted where it stands, one lifts it to another place, tilts it so the stone falls, takes what he needs, and returns it.

steps.title: Coins on a cushion: the leniency applies only when they were forgotten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of coins on a cushion. רב חייא בר אשי says in the name of רב that shaking off the coins is allowed only if they were forgotten there. If they were placed there on purpose, the cushion becomes a בסיס לדבר האסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Coins that are on a cushion.' רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: They taught this only when one forgot them there. But if he placed them there, the cushion becomes a base for a forbidden item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, coins lying on a cushion. רב limits the leniency in the same way he limited the stone on the barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows shaking the cushion so the coins fall off. רב says this works only when the coins were left there by mistake. If they were put there on purpose, the cushion takes on the forbidden status of the coins and may not be moved at all. This is the same distinction רב made in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of… (limits a ruling)
One who forgets (left it there by mistake)
One who places (put it there on purpose)
A base for a forbidden item; the base itself becomes מוקצה

steps.whatToRemember: For both the stone on the barrel and the coins on the cushion, the leniency applies only when the item was forgotten. If it was placed there on purpose, the base becomes a בסיס לדבר האסור and may not be moved.
steps.whyThisMatters: The forgot-versus-placed distinction is the key test for בסיס לדבר האסור throughout הלכות מוקצה.

phrases.english: 'Coins that are on a cushion.'
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה: he shakes the cushion and they fall.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Hiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
They taught this only where one forgets [them],
but where one places [them],
it becomes a base for a forbidden item.
phrases.notes: So the cushion may not be moved at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָעוֹת שֶׁעַל הַכַּר. אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּשׁוֹכֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה and applies the same limit רב gave in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shaking coins off a cushion is allowed only if they were forgotten there. If placed on purpose, the cushion becomes a בסיס לדבר האסור and may not be moved.

steps.title: Shaking is only for when you need the cushion itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה's rule of shaking off the coins applies only when you need the cushion itself. If you need its place, you may move it with the coins still on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The rule of shaking off the coins applies only when you need the cushion itself. But if you need the cushion's place, you may move it with the coins still on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the משנה's rule about shaking coins off a cushion. It depends on why you want to move the cushion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you want to sit on or use the cushion, you shake off the coins and take the cushion. If you only need the space where it sits, shaking would just leave the coins in that same spot. So in that case you may carry the whole cushion away with the coins still on it.

keyTerms.meaning: For the use of the object itself
Because you need the space it takes up
They only taught this rule in a case of...

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that needing the place is a stricter case. It is actually more lenient here: you do not have to shake off the coins at all. You simply carry the cushion away with them.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
They only taught this when it is needed for the item itself,
but if it is needed for its place —
phrases.notes: He needs the spot where the cushion is lying.

phrases.english: he moves it while they (the coins) are still on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְצוֹרֶךְ גּוּפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another limit to the משנה's case of coins on a cushion, after רב's limit about forgotten coins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shaking off the coins applies when you need the cushion itself. When you need its place, you may move it with the coins on it.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same rule
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב of Difti taught a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise חייא בר רב of Difti taught: The rule of shaking applies only when you need the cushion itself. But if you need its place, you may move it with the coins still on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא says the same thing as רבי יוחנן, word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וְכֵן ('and likewise') tells us this is support, not a new idea. רבי יוחנן's distinction is not only his own opinion. It also appears in a taught source.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise it was taught (introduces a supporting source)

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן תָּנֵי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּיפְתִּי:
phrases.english: And likewise Ḥiyya bar Rav from Difti taught:
They only taught this when it is needed for the item itself,
but if it is needed for its place —
he moves it while they are still on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן תָּנֵי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּיפְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's statement with a matching ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's distinction between needing the item and needing its place
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of חייא בר רב of Difti

steps.title: A forgotten purse may be moved by placing bread or a baby on it
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the coins case, רבי אושעיא rules that if someone forgot a purse in the courtyard, he puts a loaf or a baby on it and carries it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Coins on a cushion, he shakes it off, etc.' רבי אושעיא said: If someone forgot a purse in the courtyard, he places a loaf of bread or a baby on it and moves it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's coin case again and attaches a new ruling about a forgotten purse of money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The purse is מוקצה because of the money inside. When you put bread or a baby on it, the purse now holds something permitted, which you are allowed to move. So you may carry the purse along with that permitted item.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not make money stop being מוקצה. The money is still מוקצה. The permitted item on top simply allows the purse to be moved, and only in a case of forgetting.

phrases.english: (The משנה said:) Coins that are on a cushion, he shakes it, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the משנה again to attach new rulings to it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
If one forgot a purse in the courtyard —

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחַ עָלֶיהָ כִּכָּר אוֹ תִּינוֹק וּמְטַלְטְלָהּ.
phrases.english: he places a loaf or a baby on it and moves it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָעוֹת שֶׁעַל הַכַּר מְנַעֵר וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's coin case and opens a new topic: moving forgotten מוקצה by placing a permitted item on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A forgotten purse may be moved by putting a loaf or a baby on it.

steps.title: The same applies to a forgotten brick
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק gives the same ruling for a brick forgotten in the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק said: If someone forgot a brick in the courtyard, he places a loaf or a baby on it and moves it.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives the same ruling, this time for a brick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brick is מוקצה because it is building material, not because it is valuable like money. This shows the method works for different kinds of מוקצה, not only money.

phrases.english: Rav Yitzḥak said:
If one forgot a brick in the courtyard —

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחַ עָלֶיהָ כִּכָּר אוֹ תִּינוֹק, וּמְטַלְטְלָהּ.
phrases.english: he places a loaf or a baby on it, and moves it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק שָׁכַח לְבֵינָה בֶּחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same method as רבי אושעיא to a different object.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A forgotten brick may be moved by placing a loaf or a baby on it.

steps.title: A story: רבי יוחנן allowed moving a forgotten saddlebag of coins
steps.stepSummary: Once a saddlebag full of coins was forgotten in the main street. רבי יוחנן ruled that people could place a loaf or a baby on it and move it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בר שילא said in the name of רבי אסי: Once people forgot a saddlebag full of coins in the main street. They came and asked רבי יוחנן, and he told them: Put a loaf or a baby on it, and move it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case where רבי יוחנן ruled exactly like the earlier statements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story backs up the method with a practical ruling from a great authority. It also shows the method was used even for a large amount of money left in a public street.

keyTerms.meaning: A main street or public road

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda bar Sheila said that Rabbi Asi said:
Once they forgot
a saddlebag full of coins in the main street,
and they came and asked Rabbi Yoḥanan,
and he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: הַנִּיחוּ עָלֶיהָ כִּכָּר אוֹ תִּינוֹק, וְטַלְטְלוּהָ.
phrases.english: Place a loaf or a baby on it, and move it.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּעַם אַחַת שָׁכְחוּ דִּסַקַּיָּא מְלֵאָה מָעוֹת בִּסְרַטְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical case that supports the loaf-or-baby method.
steps.raayaObject: The method of moving forgotten מוקצה by placing a loaf or a baby on it
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real ruling by רבי יוחנן, reported by רבי אסי

steps.title: The הלכה follows these rulings only when the item was forgotten
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא rules that all these statements are the הלכה, but only when the item was forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: The הלכה follows all these statements, but only for someone who forgot.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives a final ruling on the loaf-or-baby method and limits it to forgotten items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone left the item outside on purpose before שבת, he may not use this trick. The leniency is only for a person who made an honest mistake.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
The halacha follows all these teachings in the case of one who forgets.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכְתָא כְּכׇל הָנֵי שְׁמַעְתָּתָא בְּשׁוֹכֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the three statements above and limits them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The loaf-or-baby method is allowed only for someone who forgot the item, not for someone who left it there on purpose.

steps.title: רב אשי: the method works only for a dead body
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי disagrees. Even when the item was forgotten, the loaf-or-baby method is not allowed. It was only permitted for moving a dead body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even someone who forgot may not do this. They allowed the loaf or the baby only for a dead body.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects the leniency for forgotten items and limits the method to one case: a dead body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a dead body may be moved on שבת by placing a loaf or a baby on it, because of respect for the dead. רב אשי says that special rule cannot be stretched to purses, bricks, or other ordinary items, even if they were forgotten.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows two opposing approaches to the method. מר זוטרא allows it for anything forgotten. רב אשי keeps it only for the special case of a dead body.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Even one who forgets also may not —
and they did not say 'a loaf or a baby'
except for a dead body alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא אָמְרוּ כִּכָּר אוֹ תִּינוֹק אֶלָּא לְמֵת בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with מר זוטרא's ruling and narrows the method even more.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of the loaf-or-baby method for any object other than a dead body, even when the object was forgotten
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The method was originally given only for a dead body, so it cannot be applied to ordinary objects.

steps.title: אביי and רבא used the method in practice
steps.stepSummary: אביי would put a spoon on bundles, and רבא would put a knife on a young dove, so they could move these things.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי would place a spoon on bundles. רבא would place a knife on a young dove and move it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what אביי and רבא actually did. This sets up רב יוסף's criticism in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They placed a permitted utensil on an item and then moved the two together. The key point is that they did this on purpose, not because something was forgotten. The next steps show why.

phrases.english: Abaye would place a spoon on bundles.
Rava would place a knife on a young dove
and move it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי מַנַּח כַּפָּא אַכִּיפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the method used in practice, setting up the criticism that follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי and רבא would place a permitted utensil on an item in order to move it.

steps.title: רב יוסף objects to using the method on purpose
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף mocks this practice. The rabbis allowed the method only when something was forgotten, not as a plan from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: How sharp is this children's teaching! Granted, the rabbis said this for someone who forgot. But did they say it may be done from the start?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף sharply criticizes what אביי and רבא did. He says the method is only for forgotten items, not for planning ahead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His point matches מר זוטרא: the leniency exists only for someone who made a mistake. Putting a spoon or knife on something on purpose, just to get around the rule, turns a leniency into a trick, so it is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, as a first choice

steps.whatToRemember: The loaf-or-baby method is a narrow leniency. מר זוטרא allows it only for forgotten items. רב אשי allows it only for a dead body. רב יוסף says nobody may use it on purpose from the start.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף's word 'sharp' is not praise. It is sarcasm: he is saying this is a childish kind of cleverness.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
How sharp is the teaching of children!
phrases.notes: Sarcastic criticism.

phrases.english: Granted, the Sages said this for one who forgets,
but did they say it may be done from the start?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן בְּשׁוֹכֵחַ לְכַתְּחִילָּה מִי אֲמוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the practice of אביי and רבא described in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of אביי and רבא, who placed utensils on items on purpose in order to move them
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The method was allowed only for someone who forgot. Using it on purpose from the start goes beyond what the rabbis permitted.

steps.title: אביי explains why he put a spoon on the bundles
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers רב יוסף. The bundles could be moved anyway because they are fit to lean on. He added the spoon only because he is an אדם חשוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If I were not an important person, why would I need a spoon on the bundles? The bundles are fit to lean on anyway!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends himself against רב יוסף's mockery. He explains that the bundles were never forbidden to move, so the spoon was not a real trick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף thought אביי was using the spoon to get around the rules for real מוקצה. אביי answers that for an ordinary person the bundles are not מוקצה at all, since they are fit to lean on. He could have moved them even without the spoon. As an אדם חשוב, though, he was strict with himself so that people would not learn from him to be lenient with forbidden things, so he added the spoon.

keyTerms.meaning: An important person (a leader whose actions people copy)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not using the spoon to move something everyone agrees is מוקצה. The bundles are usable for ordinary people. He added the spoon only as an extra stringency, because people who watch an אדם חשוב might learn to be lenient.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If not for the fact that I am an important person,
phrases.notes: People copy an important person, so he is strict with himself.

phrases.english: why would I need a spoon on the bundles?
They are fit to lean on!
phrases.notes: Because the bundles have a use, they are not מוקצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו דְּאָדָם חָשׁוּב אֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's mockery in step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: The item is permitted for ordinary people; the spoon was added only as a stringency for an important person whom others copy
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי was using the spoon method on purpose to move מוקצה
steps.terutzMaskana: For an ordinary person the bundles are usable and not מוקצה. אביי added the spoon only because, as an אדם חשוב, he was strict with himself so others would not learn leniency. This is not the deliberate trick רב יוסף objected to.

steps.title: רבא explains why he put a knife on the young dove
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the same kind of answer. The young dove could be moved anyway because it can be eaten raw. He added the knife only because he is an אדם חשוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If I were not an important person, why would I need a knife on the young dove? It is fit for me to eat as raw meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his own practice the same way אביי did. The dove was already allowed to be moved, so the knife was not really needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slaughtered young dove can be eaten raw, so for an ordinary person it is food and not מוקצה. רבא added the knife only because, as an אדם חשוב, he was strict with himself so others would not learn leniency. Notice the reason רבא gives: the dove is fit for a person to eat raw. The next step builds on this.

phrases.english: Rava said: I, too,
if not for the fact that I am an important person —
why would I need a knife on a young dove?
It is fit for me to eat as raw meat.
phrases.notes: Notice רבא's reason: it's fit for a person. The גמרא is about to look at that next.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אֲנָא, אִי לָאו דְּאָדָם חָשׁוּב אֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel answer to אביי's answer in step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: The item is permitted for ordinary people; the knife was added only as a stringency for an important person whom others copy
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא was using the knife method on purpose to move מוקצה
steps.terutzMaskana: The dove is fit for ordinary people to eat raw and so is not מוקצה. רבא added the knife only because, as an אדם חשוב, he was strict with himself so others would not learn leniency.

steps.title: Inference that רבא agrees with רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: From רבא's reason, the גמרא infers that if the dove were not fit for a person, he could not move it. It asks: does רבא hold like רבי יהודה?
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that it is fit to eat raw. This implies that if it were not fit to eat raw, it could not be moved. Does that mean רבא holds like רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רבא's words closely and draws an inference. This step sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the dove may be moved because a person can eat it raw. That suggests that being fit only for animals would not be enough. This matches רבי יהודה, who forbids moving food meant for people that is now fit only for animals. So the גמרא asks whether רבא really holds this view.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is (signals an inference from the reason given)
Is that to say? (introduces a questioned conclusion)

phrases.english: The reason is that it is fit to be eaten as raw meat;
but if it were not fit to be eaten as raw meat — no, it could not be moved.
Is that to say that Rava
holds like Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה forbids moving human food that is now fit only for animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דַּחֲזֵי לְאוּמְצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the exact wording of רבא's reason in step 25
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבא agree with רבי יהודה that food fit only for animals may not be moved?

steps.title: Challenge from רבא's instruction about the duck
steps.stepSummary: רבא told his attendant to roast a duck and throw its intestines to the cat. That shows he lets people move food fit only for animals, which goes against רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא told his attendant: Roast a duck for me, and throw its intestines to the cat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference from the previous step by quoting another statement of רבא. In that statement he clearly allows moving food that is fit only for animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The duck's intestines were not human food, yet רבא let the attendant move them to feed the cat. So רבא does not agree with רבי יהודה. If so, he should have said the dove may be moved because a dog can eat it, so why did he need the reason that a person can eat it raw?

keyTerms.meaning: But did he not say? (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say to his attendant:
phrases.notes: This was said on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Roast a duck for me,
and throw its intestines to the cat.
phrases.notes: Moving the intestines for the cat was allowed, which does not fit רבי יהודה's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רָבָא לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference in step 26 using another statement of רבא
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that רבא holds like רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא let the duck's intestines be moved for the cat, so he allows moving food fit only for animals. That contradicts the inference from his reason about the dove.
